name: QUIC Network Simulator
what_it_is: An ns-3-based test framework that benchmarks QUIC protocol implementations by routing traffic between Docker-containerized client and server endpoints through a simulated network. It enables controlled evaluation of QUIC performance under configurable link conditions such as bandwidth, delay, and queue size.
components: Two isolated Docker bridge networks (leftnet, rightnet)
Shared log volumes per service under ./logs/
measurement: Logs written to ./logs/sim, ./logs/server, ./logs/client for post-run analysis
No built-in real-time throughput or latency measurement tooling documented
configuration: CLIENT: image name of the client QUIC implementation (required)
SERVER: image name of the server QUIC implementation (required)
SCENARIO: scenario name plus parameters passed to ns-3 (required)
CLIENT_PARAMS: extra CLI arguments forwarded to the client container (optional)
SERVER_PARAMS: extra CLI arguments forwarded to the server container (optional)
ROLE: injected automatically as 'client' or 'server' into each endpoint container
NET_ADMIN capability granted to all containers
IP masquerading disabled on both networks
fault_injection: TCP cross-traffic competing with QUIC flows (tcp-cross-traffic scenario)
Queue saturation via small --queue value to induce packet drops
Artificial bandwidth cap via --bandwidth to create congestion
modes: simple-p2p: point-to-point link with configurable bandwidth, delay, and queue
tcp-cross-traffic: point-to-point link with a competing TCP flow
constraints: Client and server must be pre-built Docker images conforming to the quic-interop-runner interface; arbitrary binaries cannot be dropped in
Only two scenarios are provided out of the box (simple-p2p, tcp-cross-traffic); custom scenarios require writing ns-3 C++ code and rebuilding the sim image
Network topology is fixed: single bottleneck link between leftnet and rightnet; multi-path or mesh topologies are not supported
No packet-loss rate or jitter parameters exposed in documented scenarios
IPv6 is enabled but no IPv6-specific test scenarios are documented
docker_services: sim (martenseemann/quic-network-simulator, ns-3 simulator, bridges leftnet and rightnet, port 57832)
server (image: $SERVER, attached to rightnet at 193.167.100.100 / fd00:cafe:cafe:100::100)
client (image: $CLIENT, attached to leftnet at 193.167.0.100 / fd00:cafe:cafe:0::100)
notable_absences: No packet loss rate parameter in the documented scenarios
No built-in traffic capture or pcap export documented
No support for more than one bottleneck link or multi-hop topologies
No CI/CD integration or result aggregation tooling in the repo itself
